title: Panipat on Makar Sankranti
subtitle: On the cold sun of Makar Sankranti, an empire gambles everything on an empty stomach
region: Delhi, Panipat, Awadh, Rohilkhand and Pune
moral: Ambition without supplies and allies can become tragedy.

sources.citation: Kashi Raja's Bakhar, eyewitness account from Shuja-ud-Daula's circle
sources.note: Often treated as the strongest primary narrative for the battle.

sources.citation: James Grant Duff, A History of the Marathas, Vol. II (1826)
sources.note: Early history using survivor testimony, valuable but colonial in perspective.

sources.citation: Uday S. Kulkarni, Solstice at Panipat: 14 January 1761 (2011)
sources.note: Recent synthesis using primary narratives and later scholarship.

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a battlefield plain under a pale winter sun

dialogue.text: Panipat, 14 January 1761: Sadashivrao Bhau leads a starving empire into one last, burning throw of the dice.

panels.shot: slow aerial drift over a parched camp at dawn

dialogue.text: For months the northern Maratha army lay trapped near Panipat, hemmed in by Afghan horse and cut from grain, grass and aid.

panels.shot: medium close-up inside a command tent, lantern light flickering

dialogue.text: Sadashivrao Bhau had taken Delhi the year before, but found no lasting allies, no reliable revenue, only enemies circling closer.

panels.shot: tight close-up on Sadashivrao Bhau’s eyes, reflecting a dim campfire

dialogue.text: Behind his guns trailed a city on the move—families, traders, servants—each extra mouth another grain of sand slipping from his hand.

panels.shot: low-angle interior shot as Bhau rises to his feet, decision made

dialogue.text: Afghan riders swept the countryside. Najib-ud-Daula and Shuja-ud-Daula sealed the rivers. The Maratha granaries stood empty.

panels.shot: medium shot of Bhau stepping out of the tent into grey morning

dialogue.speaker: sadashivrao_bhau
dialogue.text: We break this ring today, or we wither behind it.

panels.shot: wide shot of the Afghan-Durrani camp across the plain, dawn haze

dialogue.text: Opposite stood Ahmad Shah Durrani, his Afghan and Rohilla horse fresh, his lines supplied by the Ganga plains and his allies’ treasuries.

panels.shot: dynamic tracking shot along Maratha artillery line facing the Afghan camp

dialogue.text: Between these camps lay the field, marked by trenches and guns—especially the disciplined infantry and artillery of Ibrahim Khan Gardi, the sharp edge of Bhau’s hope.

panels.shot: wide, almost overhead shot of the Maratha battle array forming at sunrise

dialogue.text: On Makar Sankranti’s dawn, Bhau chose to burst the noose—advance with all, crush the Afghan center, and carry his starving host southward through blood.

panels.shot: medium close on a gaunt Maratha foot-soldier adjusting his turban, resolved

dialogue.text: Men who had chewed on boiled leather now tightened belts and wrapped ragged shawls, readying themselves for one clear task—break through or die standing.

panels.shot: low, dramatic shot of Ibrahim Khan Gardi’s battalion and guns firing

dialogue.text: At first the plan held. Ibrahim Khan Gardi’s guns and drilled lines tore into the Afghan van, checking even the famous Abdali cavalry.

panels.shot: wide shot showing Afghan cavalry veering around the Maratha flank in dust

dialogue.text: But the enemy did not only charge the front. Light Afghan and Rohilla horse skirted the flanks, harassing, probing, waiting for any break in formation.

panels.shot: heroic low-angle of Sadashivrao Bhau atop his elephant in the center

dialogue.text: Bhau himself rode forward with the household troops and elephants, pressing the center hard, trusting his artillery and infantry to hold the line behind.

panels.shot: medium wide of the Maratha right wing, cavalry pressed and wavering

dialogue.text: Yet as the hours dragged, the overloaded Maratha wings began to fray. Horses lacked fodder; men lacked reserves. Order thinned into patches of desperate courage.

panels.shot: close on a Maratha gun position as ammunition boxes lie nearly empty

dialogue.text: Powder and shot ran low. Months of blockade had starved not only bellies but wagons and animals; every round fired that day had been carried at great cost.

panels.shot: wide shot of battlefield at midday haze, piles of abandoned gear and swirling cavalry

dialogue.text: The Afghan king used his strength carefully, feeding in fresh troops, conserving his fire, while Bhau had brought almost everything onto the field at once.

panels.shot: intense close-up of a young nobleman on horseback identified by royal finery

dialogue.text: Amid that storm rode Vishwasrao, the Peshwa’s heir, close to Bhau. In the crush of men and elephants, a shot found him; the hope of Pune fell in an instant.

panels.shot: medium shot of Sadashivrao Bhau on his elephant hearing the news, shoulders sagging

dialogue.text: When word of Vishwasrao’s death reached Bhau, it struck at the very heart of his army, already stretched, already fighting on emptiness and memory.

panels.shot: dramatic side shot of Bhau dismounting from his elephant amid chaos

dialogue.text: Accounts tell of Bhau leaving his elephant to fight among his soldiers on foot, trying to rally a center now sagging under repeated Afghan blows.

panels.shot: low wide shot of exhausted Maratha infantry locked in close melee, faces strained

dialogue.text: The close of the day became a press of bodies and will. Ammunition spent, many fought hand to hand, their formations collapsing into clumps of last stands.

panels.shot: wide aerial shot of the Maratha lines breaking and flowing backward

dialogue.text: Once the line broke in places, Afghan horse poured through, rolling up units from the rear, while weary Maratha wings could no longer close the breaches.

panels.shot: somber medium shot of Bhau fighting amid a knot of loyal guards, silhouettes

dialogue.text: In the tangle of dust and steel, Bhau vanished. Most sources hold that he fell there, around his personal guard; later stories of escape remain unproven.

panels.shot: wide twilight shot of the battlefield strewn with discarded weapons and silent forms

dialogue.text: By nightfall, the Maratha host was shattered. Chroniclers speak of tens of thousands lost, though exact numbers drift between memory and fear.

panels.shot: medium wide of captured Maratha soldiers herded under guard, heads bowed

dialogue.text: Kashi Raja’s account from Shuja-ud-Daula’s camp describes prisoners taken and many later slain, a grim reprisal in the flush of victory.

panels.shot: interior shot of Ahmad Shah Durrani’s tent, maps and spoils laid out

dialogue.text: Ahmad Shah Durrani had checked Maratha expansion in the north, but his own empire was a tapestry of distant tribes; he withdrew, leaving a wounded, contested heartland behind.

panels.shot: melancholic wide shot of Pune’s skyline imagined, with newsbearer arriving at dusk

dialogue.text: In Pune, the news fell like a monsoon of ash. The Peshwa’s court, built on a decade of victories, suddenly faced widowhood, succession and questions of blame.

panels.shot: medium shot of a scholar in later years reading a bakhar manuscript by lamplight

dialogue.text: Bakhars, colonial histories and modern studies all trace many causes—starvation, broken alliances, heavy non-combatants, and a confederacy whose parts could not pull together on that one cold day.

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot of the sun rising over the Deccan hills years later

dialogue.text: Yet Panipat was not an end. The Marathas rebuilt, learned, and would again shape the subcontinent, carrying the scar of that Sankranti as a warning stitched into power’s cloth.
